To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DiSC assay can be used to investigate mechanisms of drug resistance in CLL, that treatment with alkylators and antimetabolites induces pleiotropic drug sensitivities or resistance in patients, that treatment with anthracyclins induces greater resistance than treatment with alkylating agents, and that patients treated with two or more regimens have significantly reduced survival.

ex vivo analysis of pleiotropic drug response in CLL patients reveals that treatment with chlorambucill, cyclophosmamide, anthrancyline, or fludrabine induces resistance to multiple cytotoxic agents and that this resistance is not associated with any known mechanism.
the DiSC assay provides a means of identifying drug resistance induced by cytotoxic agents and can be used to develop treatment protocols for CLL.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel strategies for the treatment of drug-resistant cancers, such as CLL.
the development and application of a novel assay for the analysis of drug sensitivity in fresh CLL lymphocytes.
the development of drug response assays to guide the selection of individualized treatment strategies in CLL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ex vivo DiSC assay data provides a useful tool for the development of novel treatment strategies and a rationale for the use of novel drugs in CLL.
drug-induced resistance is complex and unpredictable.
the DiSC assay is a useful tool for the analysis of drug resistance in CLL and other hematologic malignancies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DiSC assay can provide a useful ex vivo model for studying the mechanisms of drug resistance, and can be applied to individual patient management.
drug resistance is a complex process that involves multiple mechanisms and that drug resistance modifiers should be administered in a sequence that minimizes pleiotropic drug-resistance.
ex vivo analysis of drug resistance in CLL provides a rationale for the development of treatment strategies and that this model is a useful system for investigating mechanisms of drug resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ex vivo DiSC assay is a useful tool for monitoring drug response in individual patients.
ex vivo drug resistance and drug sensitivity profiles of fresh patient samples can be used to guide therapy.
the ex vivo DiSC assay can be used to identify drug resistance induced by treatment, and to identify drug resistance modifiers.
